A day or two later in Glas, a regional newspaper, featured his official report in which he stated that an attempt had been prepared against his life in Prijedor which he allegedly barely avoided which, of course, was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time to stop?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Keegan, it would be. The Trial Chamber would like to discuss a matter with counsel. So, Dr. Mujadzic, you are excused for the day. You should return tomorrow at 10 a.m. and we will resume your testimony then (The witness withdrew).

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, the Prosecutor has filed a notification under Rule 67(A)(i) of the Tribunal's Rules and it had to do with the requirement that you list rebuttal witnesses ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- in response to the Defence's notice of alibi. That has been served on the Defence, has it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, it has.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Basically what you say in the notification is that you are unable to determine the specifics of the testimony of the alibi witnesses, that because of that you are unable to provide a complete list of the rebuttal witnesses or, indeed, any rebuttal witnesses, and that the Prosecution will notify the Defence as soon as it determines the rebuttal witnesses it intends to call. Have I correctly stated the essence of the notice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Essentially the position is, your Honours, that some of the witnesses that we will call in-chief may address some of these issues which may be raised by the Defence in their defence, but we have no other witnesses that we can call or have identified at this stage who would expressly address in rebuttal the defence of alibi, the witnesses that the Defence will call in alibi. Essentially, we cannot do that because we have not been able to get specific enough detail to do it. It may be that even if we had the specific detail we still may not be able to locate such people, but we found it difficult to obtain any useful information or any useful assistance from the people that we would consult on the basis of the information that we have at the moment in terms of identifying rebuttal witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The concern of the Trial Chamber was that this was just a notice that was filed or notification, and it really did not require any action on the part of the Trial Chamber. But it seemed, at least from our reading of the notification, that you should either file a motion for additional time to comply with the Rule and provide the Defence with your rebuttal witnesses, or you should file a motion for a more specific designation, I suppose, by the Defence as to its alibi witnesses. What I am trying to say is that this was just a notification basically advising the Chamber that you would not be complying with the deadline, because we had set a deadline for you to provide the Defence with the rebuttal witnesses. I think we are concerned that if later you attempt to offer rebuttal witnesses there will be a question of timeliness. So, if it is your intention just to notify the Chamber, that is fine, but if it is your intent to say that, at this time, we want additional time because we cannot respond because of the lack of specificity or, better yet, probably a motion requesting the Defence to be more specific in its alibi notice, because there is nothing that we can do other than to receive the notice and I am afraid it is just deferring a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Your Honour, it was not intended to convey the impression that we were not intending to comply.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What we wished to convey was that at this stage we had no such witnesses and we did go on to specify the reasons, or some of the reasons, why we did not have such witnesses. I take what your Honour has said, and certainly we will give consideration for filing a motion to address it. We do envisage that problems could arise because of the lack of specificity, and it may be that it is appropriate to deal with that by way of motion. If further specificity is available, it may assist us in locating rebuttal witnesses. The only other way around it we would envisage would be that once the witness had given testimony we may in a desperate attempt at that stage be looking around to see whether there were rebuttal witnesses, but that is a clumsy and perhaps a time-consuming process. Certainly, your Honours, we are quite happy to deal with it by way of motion to raise the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. I think that would be appropriate because 67(A)(i) provides that you give the Defence any rebuttal witnesses that you have with respect to the alibi defence, and we set a time limit for it. If you cannot meet that time limit you either have to get an extension of time or we are going to have to resolve the problem of at least your contention that the alibi defence notification is not specific. Do you have anything to say, Mr. Wladimiroff, to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just a little, your Honour. Since the Prosecution has interviewed our client on two occasions quite detailed, we believe that all the details the Prosecution is looking for will be found in his statement. The same names as we provided for in the notice will be found in his statement which is in the possession of the Prosecution since last summer and last December. So we think the Prosecution has lots of details which enable it to do what it should do. The second thing I want to address your Court on is, is it not the idea for the Prosecution to interview the alibi witnesses and to find what they should do by hearing what those witnesses are able to say? They have got the names and addresses. So we think we have complied with all we had to do.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We have not reviewed, of course we have not even received, the statement of your client. So I do not know how specific that is. That is the kind of thing we might receive by way of a motion. They say in their notification that they do not have enough details. What they are saying, I guess, is that although names have been given, they do not know when that person is supposed to be an alibi witness for the Defence. That is the names given.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is his statement.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I would guess if they look at the statement or maybe if they go and talk to these people whose names are listed, that is a way to get more details about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I understand, your Honour, but once again the Defence takes the position that all this kind of information will be found in the statement of Mr. Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It may be, and that is why I am suggesting that the Prosecutor bring that to our attention. Right now all we have is a notification that they have not met a deadline that we set. What I am saying is if they do not meet that deadline and later down the line they attempt to offer rebuttal witnesses, they are going to be in a very difficult position without some leave of the Trial Chamber. So, what I am saying is that they need to bring that on to us. If they file a motion saying that it is not specific enough for them to list rebuttal witnesses, you will then respond by saying just what you have said. You have the statement, perhaps even attach the statement to your response. You have the names of the witnesses. You go and talk to them and we will then rule on it. Right now we cannot do anything other than have this piece of paper and we are afraid that later down the line there is going to be a big battle between you two sets of lawyers and we are trying to avoid it. That is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We will just see what happens when they file their motion.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. You will file that by next Wednesday. Can you do that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We will stand adjourned until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (The court adjourned until the following day). 19 21 22 23 24 25
